hints: Focus on which functional group actually undergoes addition with HCN in the presence of cyanide catalyst.
Remember that HCN addition adds exactly one extra carbon from the CN group, so work backwards from 4 carbons in R to find carbons in Q.
Check each structure to find a 3-carbon molecule with a C=O that can be attacked by cyanide, then see which one fits perfectly.
walkthrough:
**Recall the HCN addition reaction**

Great start, let's remember the key reaction. Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition with HCN to form hydroxynitriles called cyanohydrins.

General equation:
$$\text{R}_2\text{C=O} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C(OH)(CN)}$$

**Use the carbon count to find Q**

Notice that the CN group brings one new carbon into the product. So product R has one more carbon than starting carbonyl Q.

Calculation rule:
$$\text{carbons in Q} = \text{carbons in R} - 1 = 4 - 1 = 3$$
So Q must be a 3-carbon aldehyde or ketone.

**Count carbons and identify functional groups**

Let's check the options. Option A is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, propanoic acid with 3 carbons but a carboxylic acid. Option B is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$, butan-2-one with 4 carbons. Option C is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, 1-chlorobutane with 4 carbons. Option D is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, propanal with 3 carbons and an aldehyde group.

**Conclude the correct Q**

Only a 3-carbon aldehyde or ketone will give a 4-carbon cyanohydrin. Propanal reacts as follows:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$$
The product has 3 + 1 = 4 carbons, exactly as required.

options.A: Incorrect. This is propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. Carboxylic acids do not undergo nucleophilic addition with HCN to form cyanohydrins, so no reaction of this type occurs.
options.B: Incorrect. This is butan-2-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$, a 4-carbon ketone. It would react with HCN, but the product would contain 5 carbons (4 + 1), not 4. Students choosing this forget to subtract the added CN carbon.
options.C: Incorrect. This is 1-chlorobutane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$. Halogenoalkanes undergo substitution or elimination, not HCN addition, and it already has 4 carbons so addition would give 5.
options.D: Correct. This is propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, a 3-carbon aldehyde. Aldehydes react readily with HCN to give a cyanohydrin, adding one carbon to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$ with 4 carbons in total.
